sources_short: Sentinel-2 L2A (Copernicus/ESA via Microsoft Planetary Computer), ESA WorldCover 2021, OpenStreetMap, GBIF

indicators.label: Tree cover (shelter)
indicators.how: Share of the 200 m square covered by trees (ESA WorldCover, 10 m).
indicators.why: Deer and boar rest and hide in woodland; on hot days woodland is the best shade (Biological Conservation 2025, roe deer).

indicators.label: Forest–open edge
indicators.how: Length of boundary between trees and grass, crops or shrubs, within 600 m (3 × 3 squares), scaled to the region.
indicators.why: Edges put food (open land) next to cover (forest): the classic roe deer habitat. Rated "high" in the feasibility study.

indicators.label: Food on open land
indicators.how: Mean Sentinel-2 NDVI of grass, crop and shrub pixels within 600 m on 24 Jul 2026 (0.25 → 0, 0.75 → 100).
indicators.why: Green, growing vegetation near cover is food. Using only open land avoids the "dark forest looks greenest" trap.

indicators.label: Quiet (far from roads)
indicators.how: Mean distance to the nearest road or built-up pixel (0 m → 0, 1 km or more → 100).
indicators.why: Hunting and recreation disturb deer more than wolves do (Ecology & Evolution 2026); tracked animals keep away from roads.

indicators.label: Water nearby
indicators.how: Distance from the square to the nearest river, stream, lake or wetland (water inside the square → 100, 400 m or more → 0).
indicators.why: Drinking water; wild boar also need wet ground to wallow in.

indicators.label: Vegetation moisture
indicators.how: Mean Sentinel-2 NDMI of vegetation in the square, scaled to the region (2nd–98th percentile).
indicators.why: Moist, lush vegetation is better food and cover in summer; dry stress lowers both. Rated "high" in the feasibility study.

indicators.label: Farmland nearby
indicators.how: Share of cropland within 600 m (50% or more → 100).
indicators.why: Wild boar raid maize and cereals next to forest; crops are also roe deer food.

indicators.label: Habitat variety
indicators.how: Shannon diversity of land-cover types (forest, shrub, grass, crop, water, wetland) within 600 m; four evenly mixed types → 100.
indicators.why: More habitat types close together support more species (landscape heterogeneity).

indicators.label: Natural cover
indicators.how: Share of the square that is forest, shrub, grassland, water or wetland (not crops, not built-up, not bare).
indicators.why: Semi-natural land holds more species than arable fields or towns.

indicators.label: Plant variety (spectral)
indicators.how: Spread (standard deviation) of Sentinel-2 NDVI across the vegetation in the square, scaled to the region.
indicators.why: More variety of greenness in an image tends to mean more plant variety (spectral variation hypothesis).

roe_deer.label: Roe deer · expert
roe_deer.rationale: Roe deer are edge animals: they feed on open land and hide in nearby woodland, so the forest–open edge gets the largest weight, then cover and food. Quiet reflects avoidance of roads and people; water and moisture matter less.
roe_deer.description: Roe deer habitat score v1 (expert weights): forest–open edge, cover, food on open land, quiet, moisture and water.

roe_deer_data.label: Roe deer · data
roe_deer_data.rationale: Weights learned from where roe deer were actually reported: each indicator that separates the 2009–2021 sightings from the rest of the region gets a weight in proportion to how well it does (indicator AUC − 0.5). It is then tested on the 2022–2026 sightings it never saw.
roe_deer_data.description: Roe deer habitat score v1 (weights learned from GBIF sightings 2009–2021, tested on 2022–2026).
roe_deer_data.heldout: Learned from 83 sightings (before 2022); on the 103 newer sightings it never saw: AUC 0.57, 41% in the top 30% of squares (expert weights on the same sightings: AUC 0.41).

wild_boar.label: Wild boar
wild_boar.rationale: Wild boar rest in dense cover and feed in fields (maize, cereals) at night, so cover and nearby farmland get the largest weights; wet ground for wallowing and quiet come next.
wild_boar.description: Wild boar habitat score v1: cover, farmland nearby, water, quiet, moisture and edge.

biodiversity.label: Biodiversity potential
biodiversity.rationale: Biodiversity potential rewards places with many habitat types close together, a high share of semi-natural land, varied vegetation, little disturbance and water. It is a proxy for how much life a place can support, not a count of species.
biodiversity.description: Biodiversity potential v1: habitat variety, natural cover, spectral diversity, quiet and water.
biodiversity.noValidation: Not yet tested. Next step: compare with the number of species recorded in GBIF per square (biased towards towns and paths) or with field surveys.

roe_deer.source: GBIF.org occurrence search, human observations, coordinate uncertainty ≤ 250 m

wild_boar.source: GBIF.org occurrence search, human observations, coordinate uncertainty ≤ 250 m

method.lead: Each 200 m square gets ten indicators, each scaled from 0 (poor) to 100 (good). A score is the weighted average of the indicators you tick. All inputs are free, open data; nothing is invented.
method.validation: For roe deer we test the score against real sightings: 186 GBIF records (2009–2026, citizen science, location within 250 m). AUC is the chance that a square with a sighting scores higher than a random square: 0.5 = no better than random, 0.7 or more = useful. Result: the expert weights score AUC 0.41 – worse than random – because people report roe deer mostly in open farmland mosaic (55% open land in sighting squares vs 34% in the region) and rarely inside forest, where deer are hard to see. Weights learned from the 2009–2021 sightings reach AUC 0.57 on the 2022–2026 sightings they never saw: weak but real. Sightings are biased towards paths and places people visit, so treat this as a first check, not proof.
limits: Weights are expert first guesses from the literature and the feasibility study; they are not fitted to data yet.
One clear Sentinel-2 date (24 Jul 2026). Weekly updates and comparison with each place's seasonal normal come next.
ESA WorldCover is from 2021 and does not separate maize from cereals, or broadleaf from conifer forest. DLR crop and forest maps can replace it in Germany.
Roads are clipped to the region, so distances near the edge are slightly too large. Footpaths and forest tracks are not counted yet.
Wild boar has only 7 usable GBIF sightings here, so its score cannot be tested yet. Biodiversity potential has no independent test yet.
Scores are relative to this region; a 70 here is not the same as a 70 in another region.
